  2. Dragons Milk Bourbon Barrel Aged Stout by New Holland Brewery .. We shouldn't want to have a harsh atmosphere that makes users feel unwelcome or not at home, which is what happens when a new users ( <3 days old) tries to acclimate to our site and get their post removed. We should instead post a standard and positive/encouraging comment in those threads to ensure they feel more at home rather than less.

If a post or comment is 3 hours old it is already too late, the damage has been done and the OP won't be able to repost it anyway because it has already been up and seen by the users. This is similar to the reason for not removing posts with 3 or more points, as that post already has gotten the traction to get it to the attention it based on its merit deserves. Deleting such a post and asking the person to repost it in the correct format would most likely forego the possibility of that post getting that traction/attention again.

Obviously this would be a guideline where we still have discretion to remove posts if they are massively breaking the rules (vote manipulation/ spamming), but removing posts for for example a missing question mark seems to be harsh in these cases. Is such a technicallity reason enough to remove a post? Our purpose as mods is to create and sustain a subverse that has quality content and to me a missing question mark doesn't really lower the quality that much. It needs to be clear that the person is asking something in the title and a question mark often isn't necessary to see that. If a post falls under the 3-3-3 rule, then should we give its deletion a second thought and leniency before doing so?
A 3-3-3 rule: we shouldn't remove things after it is 3 hours old, has 3 or more points or if the poster has been on Voat 3 days or shorter.

I suggest that we add subverse categories to Voat!   • Gaming --> /v/pcgaming, /v/LeagueofLegends, /v/kotor
  • Sports --> /v/football, /v/Cricket, /v/golf
  • Music --> /v/ElectroSoul, /v/ndh, /v/metal
